headline: ASML's finance chief says a proposed US law limiting sales of its chip-making machines to China would backfire by speeding up China's own equipment development.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: company statement on a live export-control bill; short text.
importance_line: It signals industry resistance to tighter chip-machine export limits, which affects chip supply chains, ASML and Chinese manufacturers, though the bill has not passed.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by The Edge Malaysia, that Roger Dassen, chief financial officer of ASML, the leading maker of chip-making equipment, told reporters after the company's third-quarter results that the Match Act now before the US Congress would, if passed after the midterm elections, speed up China's development of rival lithography technology. He said he was "optimistic that common sense will prevail".
notes: Reuters link blocked; same Reuters text read on The Edge Malaysia. Pool url is mezha.net; Reuters link used for credit.
